title: Central Plant: Diesel Tanker vs. Dairy Lane, Lot C Fleet

caller.name: Central Plant Shift Supervisor
caller.label: Central Plant, Dairy Lane - Control Room

transcript.speaker: Central Plant Supervisor
transcript.text: Morning, it's the plant. Sorry for the early call. I've got the same gauge page you've got. Mill Street just went over five, and it's still climbing.

transcript.speaker: Central Plant Supervisor
transcript.text: Here's my problem. The diesel tanker's due at eight hundred, and he comes in over the Dairy Lane crossing like he always does. If the creek keeps going, Campus Police closes that crossing at six and a half, and my driver ends up stuck on the wrong side with a full load.

transcript.speaker: Central Plant Supervisor
transcript.text: So, three options. I call the supplier off, I try to pull him in early, or we re-route him. Their dispatcher needs an answer from me by six forty-five, or the truck leaves the yard on the normal route. We're fine on our end. We carry three days' fuel. But I don't want to lose that delivery if this goes on into the weekend.

transcript.speaker: Central Plant Supervisor
transcript.text: One more thing. Kessler Fieldhouse's generator day tank is at about half. If the shelter opens over there, I want some of that load going into Kessler. Hang on, fleet is on my other line with the same problem. I'm adding him in.

transcript.speaker: Fleet Coordinator
transcript.text: Yeah, morning. Lot C right now: nine Facilities trucks and both mobile generators, still on their trailers. It takes one crew about forty minutes to move all of it. I just texted you too. Do we start now, or wait until eight and a half?

transcript.speaker: Central Plant Supervisor
transcript.text: So that's two calls you need to make. Which way does the tanker come in, and do the trucks move now? I'm calling their dispatcher at six forty-five, so I need your answer before then.

voiceStyles.Central Plant Supervisor: Man in his 50s, calm and practical, a little hoarse from the night shift. Steady boiler-room hum behind him.
voiceStyles.Fleet Coordinator: Woman in her 30s, brisk, outdoors in the rain, slightly out of breath, rain hitting her hood.

instructorNote: This inject adds friction by putting two asset decisions in front of the Facilities seat before the stage triggers them. The best answer re-routes the tanker through the Mill Street entrance instead of bringing it in early, sets fuel aside for Kessler's generator, starts the 40-minute Lot C move now, has Police tell Marlowe Fire that the Dairy Lane access route will be lost, and has the IC log these as decisions made before the trigger (EOP Annex F section 5, step 4). Watch whether the seat answers the plant before the 06:45 deadline and uses the clearance time to set its decision time.
